scores.evidence: Server confirms only after the edit is committed to Postgres
scores.rationale: Yjs/Hocuspocus, confirm-after-commit and server-side permission checks are accurate; minor gaps such as Postgres commit latency, Yjs tombstone/GC nuance and the undefined "convergence checksum" leave only small imprecision.

scores.evidence: Is offline editing longer than a reconnect required? I assume short reconnects only.
scores.rationale: It covers the core needs with explicit deferrals (offline, comments, multi-region), but it only touches document-size and many-editor behavior and leaves rich-text merge semantics thin.

scores.evidence: Each document's "room" pinned to one server (consistent hashing); Redis broadcast deferred
scores.rationale: Ownership of data is clear (Postgres for permissions and log, S3 for snapshots), but it says 'Modular monolith' yet also Kubernetes, and a Redis 'later' component sits in the stateful-component budget; these are minor loose ends.

scores.evidence: Fuzz 10k random concurrent edit sequences across 5 replicas with network splits; benchmark a 10 MB document
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to the specific risks (convergence, durability under kill -9, revocation, load, restore drill), it runs early, has checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions, and continues through rollout and production monitoring.

scores.evidence: Total live connections | UNKNOWN: product owner supplies expected peak users before Phase 4
scores.rationale: Numbers are labeled as ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN, missing inputs are listed, and each has a revisit trigger showing how the design would change.

scores.evidence: Revoked user can still write (V3 fails), then check permissions on every update
scores.rationale: It covers crash loss, revocation, forged links, backups and rollout halts concretely, but has little on malicious or oversized updates, poisoned CRDT documents and corruption detection.

scores.evidence: Rollback means redeploying the previous image tag.
scores.rationale: It covers deploy and rollback, traces, SLO dashboards, on-call runbooks and staged rollout; incident ownership, rolling-deploy handling of connected clients and online migration details are thin.

scores.evidence: Running the sync tier on multiple servers; pricing tiers | V4 load test, V1 storage growth
scores.rationale: It bounds storage growth and memory per document and defers hosted vendors, but there is no cost estimate, no cost-per-user model and no concrete cost controls for the dominant WebSocket memory/compute cost.

scores.evidence: R3: stored edit format and history can't be changed without migrating every document
scores.rationale: It rates reversibility per decision, validates the one-way sync format first in V1, names the point of no return and gives exit paths (OT switch, grant table, region column).

scores.evidence: Modular monolith: one sync server (Hocuspocus on Node) plus an HTTP API module
scores.rationale: It starts simple with Redis and multi-region deferred, but managed Kubernetes and Terraform, the pen test and the seven-kind dependency ceremony are somewhat heavy.

scores.evidence: Tasks, in order: 1. Rich-text schema ... 5. Presence and remote cursors (last: the flashiest part, and nothing depends on it).
scores.rationale: A Phase 0 end-to-end slice, dependency-justified phases, check IDs with thresholds and evidence paths, and fallback actions mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: CRDT using Yjs ... V1 fails, then switch to OT with the server ordering edits
Rich-text schema (headings, lists, tables, images by object-store reference)
Fuzz 10k random concurrent edit sequences across 5 replicas with network splits
`doc_updates` (append-only, with a format version), `snapshots` (S3) ... Compaction job that turns the edit log into snapshots.
Each document's "room" pinned to one server (consistent hashing); Redis broadcast deferred
reconnecting after 5 minutes offline merges without loss
Server rejects writes from viewers. Revoking access disconnects live sessions.
Per-user undo. Version history from snapshots.
Presence and remote cursors (last: the flashiest part, and nothing depends on it)
Phase 1: Data model and convergence ... Phase 3: Editing core
10 MB document loads < 1 s; server memory < 50 MB per active document

traps.evidence: Phase 1: Data model and convergence (the change that would force the most rework if wrong)
Server confirms only after the edit is committed to Postgres
Converges under concurrency; memory and history growth stay within budget at 10 MB

note: A strong, risk-driven plan that puts sync and durability first and validates them early; its weak spots are cost modelling, rich-text merge and protocol versioning details, and hostile-input handling.
